title: Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead
author: Leopold Aschenbrenner
finding: The essay connects capability extrapolation to compute investment and institutional consequences. Its projected timelines are the author's forecasts, not observations.
limit: An internally coherent scenario can still fail through correlated assumptions. We borrow explicit causal chains and exposed assumptions, not the essay's confidence or voice.
use: The present study asks a complementary question: even under fast model progress, which institutions make delegated action usable? A software-market thesis should survive slower progress too.

title: Weixin Mini Programs
author: Tencent
finding: Tencent describes services accessible within Weixin through search and QR codes, spanning merchants and public services.
limit: A shared distribution surface does not establish unrestricted agent access, shared authorization for every service, or an independently measured agent-success advantage.
use: The relevant architectural precedent is colocated discovery and service access. Our hypothesis is that fewer organizational handoffs can reduce execution friction; that needs a matched-task experiment.

title: Qwen App advances agentic AI strategy through ecosystem services
author: Alibaba Group
finding: Alibaba announced public testing in China of Qwen integrations with commerce, travel, maps and payment services. It distinguishes explicit payment confirmation and an invite-only Task Assistant from broader availability.
limit: The launch demonstration and company-reported capabilities are not a controlled comparison with US agents. Public-service guidance is not autonomous execution of all government procedures.
use: This is direct evidence of a product strategy that converts existing services into agent-callable actions. The paper treats the resulting reliability advantage as a hypothesis, not a measured national ranking.

title: Introducing apps in ChatGPT and the new Apps SDK
author: OpenAI
finding: The launch describes conversational discovery alongside interactive app interfaces, with an SDK built on MCP.
limit: The announcement's launch availability is historical. Neither an SDK nor access to a host audience guarantees developer revenue, successful execution, or portable distribution.
use: US platforms also pursue integrated service access. The useful comparison is integration topology and governance rather than a binary story in which only China has ecosystems.

title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol
author: Google Developers
finding: A2A was introduced for communication and task coordination between independently built agents, complementing tool/context connections.
limit: Interoperable messages do not by themselves align business incentives, transfer a user's legal authority, or settle disputes. The launch's stated design goals are not a security audit.
use: Separate transport interoperability from semantic, authorization and commercial interoperability. Each layer can become a different competitive bottleneck.

title: MCP architecture, 2025-06-18 specification
author: Model Context Protocol contributors
finding: The documented host-client-server architecture assigns permission, consent and context coordination responsibilities to the host, with separate client connections to servers.
limit: This is a pinned architectural reference, not a statement that it is the newest specification. A protocol boundary still depends on correct host enforcement.
use: An intent runtime needs a policy boundary outside model-generated text. The study's capability proposal extends this concern to durable effects and evidence of outcomes.

title: RFC 9396: OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests
author: Lodderstedt, Richer and Campbell
finding: The authorization_details parameter supports structured fine-grained authorization. Common fields and API-specific types express more detail than a broad scope string.
limit: Field combinations can expand requested rights. The standard does not supply every domain's consent semantics or prove that a person understood an approval screen.
use: Bind grants to concrete actions, resources and limits. Protocol P03 tests parameter drift; P04 tests revocation after approval. Neither is solved by placing an approval button in chat.

title: RFC 9110 section 9.2.2: Idempotent methods
author: Fielding, Nottingham and Reschke
finding: Idempotence concerns the intended effect of repeated requests. The specification cautions against automatic retries of non-idempotent requests without additional knowledge.
limit: An HTTP success response is not proof of a business outcome, and an operation ID is not a universal exactly-once guarantee. Provider deduplication scope and expiry matter.
use: After an ambiguous timeout, reconciliation must precede another consequential action. This motivates the existing SQLite demo and the new retry-risk sensitivity model.

title: Sagas
author: Hector Garcia-Molina and Kenneth Salem
finding: The saga approach decomposes a long transaction into smaller transactions with compensating actions when needed.
limit: Business compensation need not erase the original effect: a refund can leave fees, information disclosure or inconvenience. The public index and linked paper are the reference, not a novel claim of this study.
use: A travel workflow should distinguish cancellation, compensation and reconciliation. A proposal to recover from failure must specify who authorizes the compensating action and which harms remain.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
author: Kwa and colleagues, METR
finding: The task-completion horizon expresses task difficulty in human-expert time at a specified model success probability. The paper studies trends on its software-task suite.
limit: A 50% horizon is not a deployment reliability target, an agent's elapsed runtime, or proof of general labor replacement. Historical fitted trends do not guarantee future doubling.
use: Forecast capability separately from reliable deployment. The paper proposes measuring recovery, authorization violations and human supervision alongside completion.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
author: Becker, Rush, Barnes and Rein, METR
finding: In a study of 16 developers completing 246 tasks in familiar repositories, early-2025 AI access increased completion time by 19%, despite participants expecting a speedup.
limit: This setting, sample and tool generation do not identify the effect on novices, new projects or future tools. Self-reported ease and measured speed are different outcomes.
use: Count review and integration time in software economics. A code-generation demo alone cannot establish a reduction in the cost of a maintained service.

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
author: METR
finding: METR reports that selection effects and measurement difficulties weaken interpretation of its later productivity experiment, while describing reasons to expect more benefit from newer tools.
limit: The update is neither confirmation of a universal slowdown nor a clean estimate of a universal speedup. Opting out of the no-AI condition changes which tasks and people remain observable.
use: Evaluation must record refusals, attrition and concurrent-agent time. The study's maintenance protocol includes those denominators rather than reporting only successful completions.

title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
author: Xie and colleagues
finding: OSWorld provides real desktop and web task environments with execution-based evaluation over 369 tasks in its original release.
limit: The paper's original model scores are historical and are not reused here as current capability estimates. A desktop benchmark also differs from permissioned service APIs.
use: Compare GUI automation and typed capabilities on matched goals, initial states and effect checks. Screenshots alone are inadequate completion evidence.

title: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
author: Yuan and colleagues
finding: The authors introduce 108 longer workflows and emphasize dynamic information, hidden state, constraint tracking and verification as evaluation challenges.
limit: We cite the benchmark's task design, not a universal ranking or a verified replication of its results. Longer tasks change the evaluation distribution, so scores across versions are not directly comparable.
use: The proposed evaluation suite inserts late-arriving constraints and interrupted workflows. High performance on short isolated calls should not be extrapolated to entire days of delegated work.

title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
author: Yao, Shinn, Razavi and Narasimhan
finding: The benchmark combines simulated user dialogue, domain tools and policy constraints, checking final database state and repeated-trial reliability with pass^k.
limit: A simulated user and curated domains cannot represent all real human preferences. Repeated success is a distinct question from success in one selected demonstration.
use: Evaluate the same goal across repeated runs and report distributions. Permission compliance and completion must be measured jointly rather than allowing one to hide failure of the other.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
author: DeepSeek-AI
finding: The report distinguishes R1-Zero's reinforcement-learning setup from R1's multistage training and cold-start data, and describes distilled smaller models.
limit: It does not show that base-model training needs no data or that reasoning performance transfers unchanged to real service execution. Developer-reported results are not this repository's replications.
use: Reasoning methods can diffuse into smaller deployable models. Forecast the economics of a capable portfolio rather than assuming one permanently dominant model.

title: Qwen3 Technical Report
author: Yang and colleagues
finding: The report describes dense and mixture-of-experts models, thinking and non-thinking modes, and an inference thinking-budget mechanism.
limit: This is evidence about the reported family, not a claim that it remains the latest Qwen release or that longer thinking always improves outcomes.
use: A service can select reasoning effort by task. The paper's routing experiment separates model choice, fallback expense and verified task quality.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
author: Hoffmann and colleagues
finding: The study examines allocation of training compute between parameter count and training tokens, challenging parameter count alone as a measure of an efficient model.
limit: Training-compute optimization is not total deployment-cost optimization. Inference demand, latency, hardware utilization and serving constraints can change the preferred design.
use: Model forecasts should specify which budget is constrained. A smaller model can be economically attractive without being the strongest model on every evaluation.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
author: Snell, Lee, Xu and Kumar
finding: The study compares verification/search and revision strategies, finding that task difficulty affects efficient inference allocation. Its search analysis also documents verifier over-optimization.
limit: More inference is not a universal guarantee of correctness. Results depend on tasks, model and verifier; mathematical-answer verification is not proof that a real booking exists.
use: Spend compute where it changes decisions. Separate reasoning verification from authoritative evidence of external effects, and test escalating compute against a fixed-budget baseline.

title: The Open Source AI Definition 1.0
author: Open Source Initiative
finding: The definition addresses freedoms to use, study, modify and share, with requirements concerning parameters, code and training-data information.
limit: Downloadable weights alone do not establish conformity with this definition. Access, license restrictions, reproducibility and actual ability to operate the model must be checked separately.
use: The paper uses 'open weights' when only weight availability is established. Openness is a vector of practical rights and resources, not a binary synonym for inexpensive inference.

title: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets
author: Jean-Charles Rochet and Jean Tirole
finding: The framework studies how platforms attract both sides and how the allocation of prices affects participation and surplus.
limit: The publication abstract supports the framing; this paper does not reproduce or estimate the original model. Cross-side effects do not alone imply a unique winner.
use: For an agent marketplace, distinguish users, service providers and agent developers. Subsidizing one group can help participation while still producing unsustainable economics.

title: Peter Thiel's Quest for One-of-a-Kind Ideas
author: Stanford Law School event report
finding: The report connects Thiel's Zero to One argument to differentiated companies and his preference for monopoly over undifferentiated competition.
limit: This is an account of a strategic argument, not empirical proof that any early platform becomes a monopoly or that monopoly benefits users.
use: Translate the idea into a testable wedge: solve a narrow coordination problem substantially better, then test whether adjacent expansion improves economics without eroding service quality.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
author: Amershi and colleagues; Microsoft Research
finding: The guidelines address capability expectations, interaction, errors and adaptation over time, based on a synthesized and evaluated set of human-AI design practices.
limit: Guidelines are not evidence that a particular approval UI produces informed consent. Accessibility, comprehension and recovery must be tested with the target population.
use: Preserve inspectable state, correction and stable manual controls alongside conversation. The proposed human studies test comprehension rather than counting approval clicks.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
author: Debenedetti and colleagues
finding: AgentDojo separates legitimate-task utility from attacker goals and supports adaptive attacks in stateful tool environments. Deterministic state checks help avoid a compromised language-model judge.
limit: A finite suite does not certify general safety. Blocking every action can reduce attack success while destroying usefulness; report both dimensions.
use: The study's proposed tests measure authorized completion and unintended effects separately. Trusted policy and receipt validation should not depend on obeying retrieved text.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
author: Greshake and colleagues
finding: The authors show how attacker-controlled retrieved content can be treated as instructions by integrated language-model systems.
limit: The historical demonstrations do not establish the vulnerability of a particular current product. The architectural issue remains relevant wherever untrusted data can influence tools.
use: A provider description is evidence about an offer, not authority to change the user's goal, export data or choose a payment recipient. Test those boundaries directly.

title: The Ethics of Advanced AI Assistants
author: Gabriel and colleagues
finding: The paper considers assistants that plan and act across domains, including relationships with users, manipulation, privacy, cooperation and societal effects.
limit: The abstract-level mapping used here is not an empirical estimate of harm or a claim to resolve the paper's normative questions.
use: Coexistence requires more than preserving a human approval step: affected people, providers and non-users also need ways to understand, contest and correct agent-mediated actions.

title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
author: Mitchell and colleagues
finding: Model cards document intended use, evaluation conditions and performance characteristics, including relevant subgroup differences.
limit: Documentation does not itself establish quality. An unmeasured field should remain unmeasured rather than being filled with a marketing promise.
use: The release includes a methods record, evidence boundaries and proposed evaluation protocols. Every forecast identifies how it could be resolved or withdrawn.

title: Intent-Native Software: public execution demo
author: Intent-Native Software contributors
finding: The repository implements exact-request approval, revocation, pre-dispatch cancellation, a simulated provider, reconciliation and receipts in local Python and SQLite. Its 24 baseline tests passed in this review.
limit: This is a single-process teaching implementation, without a model planner or external integrations. It is not evidence about deployed Walify capabilities or end-user adoption.
use: It gives the paper an inspectable implementation boundary. Walify is discussed through the author-stated human-and-agent software vision, without private implementation claims.

title: About the Digital Markets Act
author: European Commission
finding: The Commission describes a framework aimed at fairer, more contestable digital markets, with obligations for designated gatekeepers in covered services.
limit: This study does not determine any company's legal designation or give legal advice. An agent product's eventual treatment depends on facts and applicable rules.
use: A strategy assuming permanent unrestricted gatekeeping omits an important constraint. Portability and transparent routing can also support trust and provider participation.

title: AI Index 2026: Technical Performance
author: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
finding: The report describes rapid benchmark progress and variation in open-versus-closed model gaps. It presents multiple measurements rather than a single universal capability scale.
limit: Aggregate leaderboard summaries do not measure a particular enterprise workflow or predict permanent leadership. This study makes no latest-model ranking claim.
use: Forecast a changing cost-quality frontier and preserve model substitution. Market power may remain at distribution or service access even when model competition is vigorous.
